data.name: Manthan
data.gender_notes: Manthan is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Manthan refers to the mythological process of churning the ocean of milk to retrieve the Amrita or the elixir of immortality. This was a significant event in Hindu mythology involving the gods and demons working together. The name Manthan carries the meaning “Churning the ocean of milk” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Manthan usually hope their child will grow to embody churning the ocean of milk and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes unity, determination, and the pursuit of divine knowledge.
data.etymology: Manthan belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Churning the ocean of milk.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Manthan total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

vedic_reference.note: Refers to the churning of the cosmic ocean by the gods and demons to obtain the elixir of immortality, Amrita.

historical_references.reference: The churning of the ocean (Samudra Manthan) is a significant event in Hindu mythology, where the gods and demons collaborated to obtain the elixir of immortality (Amrita), using the serpent Vasuki as the churning rope and the mountain Mandara as the churning rod.
historical_references.context: This event is described in various Hindu scriptures such as the Mahabharata and the Puranas.

historical_references.reference: Manthan is also the name of a sage, who is considered one of the Saptarishis (Seven Great Sages) in Hindu mythology. He is believed to have lived during the Treta Yuga, the second of the four stages in Hindu cosmology.
historical_references.context: Manthan is revered for his wisdom and is often depicted as a sage with a serene expression and a tranquil demeanor.
